title: Grounding Language Models in Speech Does Not Fix "AI Flavor": Calibrated LLM Judges, Goodhart Traps, and a Preference-Tuning Fix
abstract: arXiv:2611.19840v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chinese outputs of large language models carry a perceptible "AI flavor": formulaic sentence frames, stacked written-register connectives, repetition loops, and layout leakage. A popular hypothesis blames text-only training for the missing inner-speech layer of human writing; injecting speech or prosody signals should therefore reduce it. We test it with controlled interventions on a 0.6B model; all three fail: (i) phoneme-interleaved continued pretraining yields no spokenness gain under text-matched controls while raising repetition (+0.13 [+0.03, +0.23]); (ii) prosody-plan conditional generation reaches an adherence of only 0.257 against a pre-registered 0.50 gate; (iii) a rule-based reward built on TTS prosody-feature distance is imperceptible in double-blind evaluation by both humans (8/16) and a calibrated LLM judge (9/16).   A root cause is evaluation: single-rater blind evaluation at n~20 only detects extreme (>=85%) preferences.

translated_title: 将语言模型与语音结合并不能消除“AI味”：校准的LLM评判器、古德哈特陷阱与一种基于偏好调优的修复方案
translated_abstract: 大语言模型的中文输出带有可感知的“AI味”：模板化的句式框架、堆叠的书面语连接词、重复循环以及排版泄漏。一种流行的假设将其归咎于纯文本训练缺失了人类写作中的“内心语音”层，因此注入语音或韵律信号应当能减少这种味道。我们在一个0.6B参数模型上通过受控干预对这一假设进行了测试，三种方法均告失败：(i) 音素交错续训在文本匹配对照下没有带来口语化提升，反而增加了重复度（+0.13 [+0.03, +0.23]）；(ii) 韵律计划条件生成的遵循度仅达到0.257，远低于预先注册的0.50门槛；(iii) 基于TTS韵律特征距离的规则奖励在人类（8/16）和校准后的LLM评判器（9/16）的双盲评估中均无法被感知。其根本原因在于评估环节：样本量约20的单评分员盲评只能检测出极端（≥85%）的偏好差异。
tldr: 该论文通过在0.6B模型上的受控实验证明，注入语音或韵律信号的三种方法（音素交错续训、韵律计划条件生成、基于TTS韵律距离的规则奖励）均无法消除LLM中文输出的“AI味”，并指出当前n≈20的单评分员盲评只能检测极端偏好的评估方法是根本症结，同时提出一种基于偏好调优的修复方案。
en_tdlr: Controlled experiments on a 0.6B model show that three speech-grounding interventions (phoneme-interleaved continued pretraining, prosody-plan conditional generation, and rule-based rewards built on TTS prosody-feature distance) all fail to reduce the “AI flavor” in Chinese LLM outputs, revealing that evaluation itself—where single-rater blind tests at n~20 only detect extreme (≥85%) preferences—is the root cause, alongside a proposed preference-tuning fix.
